newsitem.title: JAPAN: FOCUS - Nissan to make 3rd car at UK plant.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Nissan to make 3rd car at UK plant.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it would invest a further 215 million pounds ($357.1 million) in Britain to make a third car model at its plant in Sunderland, northeast England.

Nissan will create 800 direct new jobs by the year 2000 to add the third model to the production line at Nissan Motor Mfg (UK) Ltd (NMUK). The investment will be used to make production equipment such as moulds for the car.

A spokesman for Nissan, Japan's second biggest carmaker, said it would produce models in the Pulsar range, called the Almera in Europe, at the plant from 2000. The British unit had 4,000 employees as of the end of 1995.
Production of the new car is also expected to create 4,000 jobs in European car parts suppliers providing components to NMUK.

Britain welcomed the news, and Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang said: "This latest decision by Nissan marks a significant development in their presence in Europe and underlines the attractions of the UK as a place to manufacture.
"Nissan's announcement is very good news for the UK automotive industry and particularly for the northeast."
Ian Gibson, chief executive of Nissan UK, speaking on BBC Business News, said: "It is a considerable vote of confidence (for Sunderland).

"It's a successful plant and it has an extremely successful workforce and they have won the business. All the business for the new car will be new business to Europe because the car is built at present in Japan and shipped over here, so all those purchases will be incremental business," he said.
The British Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said in a statement the move would create a 2,700 jobs among UK component suppliers in addition to the 800 direct jobs at the plant.

The Nissan Europe technology centre in Britain will develop the new car. This decision follows recent announcements from Nissan that it will start building diesel engines in Sunderland in 1997, and will launch an estate version of the Primera built in Sunderland in 1998, creating 150 jobs.
NMUK produced 232,000 cars in calendar 1996, including 137,000 Micras and 95,000 Primeras. NMUK will boost its output to about 266,000 cars in 1997, the Nissan spokesman said.
Overall car production in Britain rose to 1.69 million units in 1996, the highest since 1973, with production for export at 910,000 units increasing fourfold in the last 10 years. ($1=.6021 Pound)
